div.head: II Cn 38
div.ab: Nis on ænigne timan unriht alyfed; ⁊ þeah man sceal freolstidan ⁊ fæstentidan ⁊ on freolsstowan geornlicost beorgan.
Nis on ænigne timan unriht alefed; ⁊ þeah man sceal freolstidan ⁊ on freolsstowan geornlicost beorgan.
Non est in aliquo tempore concessa iniusticia; et tamen est festis diebus et sanctificatis locis propensius interdicta.
Nis on ænigne timan unriht alyfad, ⁊ ðeah man sceal freolstídan ⁊ on freolsstowan geornlicost bebyrgan.
Nis on ænigne timan unriht alyfed; and þeah man sceal freolstidan and fæstentidan and on freolsstowan geornlicost beorgan.
Nicht zu irgend einer Zeit ist Unrecht erlaubt; man soll aber zu Festzeiten (und Fastenzeiten G) und an Orten [kirchlicher] Feier sich doch am ernstlichsten [davor] hüten.
Wrong is permitted at no time; but one must guard against it most carefully at festivals (and fasts, G) and in holy places.
Lawlessness is not permitted at any time, yet at sacred seasons and in sacred places special care must be taken to prevent it.
Wrong-doing is not permitted at any time; and yet it should be especially guarded against at festival seasons and in sacred places.
Wrongdoing shall not be tolerated at any time; yet during holy seasons and at holy places it must be suppressed with the greatest diligence.
div.note: G's ‘⁊ fæstentidan’ is missing from the others (perhaps added from the Canons of Edgar, Conf. 4). Liebermann compares the Canons of Edgar, Conf. 4.
This and the next clause are drawn from an ecclesiastical tract known as “Concerning Confession”.
The Nero text adds: “and fasting seasons”, which is also in the source.
